question: Across the seven registered build policies (wt-pure, wt-free/control, wt-partner, fuse-early, fuse-mid, fuse-late, fuse-flank) on the Magma Trap fusion, does any policy dominate the others on both mazes by more than the resolvable margin, and how do the fusion-based policies separate from wt-partner (the two-ingredient, unfused baseline) on hallHpAuc?
sigmaSource: Paired hallHpAuc delta sd measured in the R2 regime by the registered regime-r2-adoption family (docs/reviews/2026-08-15-regime-r2-adoption.md, 24,000 runs, 18/18 gates PASS): ~0.87 (maze A) / ~1.41 (maze B) across the Watchtower ladder rungs, maze B the binding constraint, reused identically by fusion-r2-magma-trap. Per docs/plans/2026-08-27-option-set-comparison-spec.md section 3, mde(sigma/sqrt(2), 750) [stats.js mde()] = 0.089 (A) / 0.144 (B) at 750 seed-cells per split side, where 750 is the size of EACH of the two random halves (S1 selection, S2 evaluation, section 2.4) the 1500 seed-cells per arm per maze (750 seeds x 2 postGaps) are drawn into for the split-sample selection procedure. mde declared above (0.144) is the maze-B, binding value at that split size.

regime.label: R2 (option-set pilot)
regime.justification: R2 (spendDown, maxWaves 10) is the standing regime, adopted 2026-08-15 on 18/18 gates and reused by every fusion-r2-* family for comparability. Isolated siting (legacySiting: false) removes the Watchtower-displacement confound documented in docs/reviews/2026-08-16-maze-split-mechanism.md. All 7 policies fix defence: WATCHTOWER and humanElement: EARTH so the only variation across arms is the what/when vector (freeSpecial, fuse, fuseWave, partnerSpecial, specialSiting) per spec section 2.1 — no new build-policy code, siting list, or defence structure is introduced.
regime.scopeLimit: This pilot runs exactly one fusion (Magma Trap, EARTH human / FIRE partner) and exactly one build policy (scripted-v1); it says nothing about any other fusion or about a competent, non-scripted human. It measures the 7-policy set registered in spec section 2.2 only — it is NOT a search over strategies (spec section 6.1) and the policy set's composition one-sidedly biases any later contribution estimator, which this pilot does not compute (that estimator, and the --option-set analyze.mjs mode, are later, separately-registered work per spec section 4). The positive-control procedure check (spec section 2.5) is a SEPARATE family, option-set-procedure-check, not part of this file.

decisionRule: This is a PILOT, not a verdict family. Its primary deliverable is the spec section 2.3 Q1 policy x maze value matrix (mean hallHpAuc, and secondarily wavesCleared, for each of the 7 policies on each maze) and the pairwise separations among them — not a single pass/fail on any one arm. Report per-pair paired deltas (each of the 6 non-control arms vs the wt-free control, which anchors analyze.mjs's CONTROL_ARM handling) with BH-adjusted q across the declared family of 24 (6 arms x 2 mazes x 2 metrics: hallHpAuc primary, wavesCleared secondary), the exact sign test, and the achieved MDE per maze (0.089 A / 0.144 B). A pair is RESOLVABLY SEPARATED when q < 0.05 AND the sign test agrees in direction AND the delta magnitude exceeds the maze's achieved MDE. 'NO TWO POLICIES SEPARATE BY MORE THAN THE RESOLVABLE MARGIN' IS A REGISTERED VALID OUTCOME OF THIS PILOT, NOT A FAILURE: it means the current 7-policy set is too narrow to answer the design question at this n, and the prescribed next step is a wider policy set or (if the pilot instead shows separation only at the small end) 1500 seeds / 42,000 runs and a re-declared nRequired — never a smaller policy set, per spec section 3. ADDING A POLICY TO THIS SET AFTER SEEING RESULTS IS PROHIBITED and invalidates this family: any later argmax-style contribution estimator over a set grown post-hoc can only be biased upward, per spec section 2.2.
whatWouldRefute: Transcribed from spec section 5 (docs/plans/2026-08-27-option-set-comparison-spec.md), all three registered before running: (1) If no fusion-building policy (fuse-early, fuse-mid, fuse-late, fuse-flank) is ever the best-performing policy on either maze, the fusion system does not pay for itself — registered here as the expected null. (2) If the separate option-set-procedure-check family's selection procedure fails to select its doubled-Watchtower-damage arm, the selection procedure itself is broken and must be published and fixed before any fusion result from this family is read. (3) If this pilot shows no two of the 7 policies separate by more than the resolvable margin (0.089 A / 0.144 B), the registered policy set is too narrow to answer the design question and the next work is a wider policy set, not a bigger n on this one.
notes:
familySize = 24, counted as (arms - 1) x mazes x (1 + secondaryMetrics) = 6 x 2 x 2, per the schema's stated default formula: 6 non-control arms (wt-pure, wt-partner, fuse-early, fuse-mid, fuse-late, fuse-flank) compared against the wt-free control, on 2 mazes, on 2 declared metrics (hallHpAuc primary + wavesCleared secondary). The wt-partner-vs-control-only comparison this produces is exploratory framing for Q2's contribution estimator (spec section 2.3) and is not itself a verdict this family issues; Q1's full 7-policy matrix is read directly off the descriptives table analyze.mjs already emits for every arm, not off these 6 pairwise comparisons alone.

CONTROL ARM NAMING. The sweep spec's armId values are wt-pure, control, wt-partner, fuse-early, fuse-mid, fuse-late, fuse-flank — the spec section 2.2 table's 'wt-free' row is named 'control' in the spec file and here, because analyze.mjs hard-codes CONTROL_ARM = 'control' (test/harness/bench/analyze.mjs:23) and the prereg schema requires arms to include a literal 'control' entry ($.arms must include control). wt-free is today's baseline (the arm every prior fusion family has graded against before the two-ingredient correction), so it is the correct semantic choice for the tool's required control slot. This is a deliberate substitution, not a typo: 'control' IS 'wt-free' throughout this family's records and this file.

nRequired = 1506 = ceil(requiredN(1.41, 0.144)) via stats.js requiredN(sigma, mde) at alpha 0.05 / power 0.8, using the maze-B (binding) paired sigma directly, matching the convention in fusion-r2-magma-trap.json. This lands almost exactly at the pilot's actual per-arm-per-maze cell count (750 seeds x 2 postGaps = 1500): requiredN(sigma/sqrt(2), mde) with mde=0.144 solves to ~750-753, and requiredN's plain (unhalved) formula is exactly double that by construction, so 1500 actual cells against nRequired 1506 confirms the pilot is sized almost exactly to the declared MDE rather than over- or under-powered by a wide margin. Maze A's requiredN(0.87, 0.089) = 1501 is nearly identical, so the two mazes' sample requirements coincide closely at these MDEs even though maze B's absolute sigma is larger.

This prereg does NOT declare a positiveControl block: the positive control (doubled Watchtower damage) lives in a separate family per spec section 2.5 (option-set-procedure-check) and must never be an arm inside this policy set, because any non-fusion arm surviving every 'remove fusion X' subset would force every future contribution() estimate to zero (spec section 0.1).

AMENDMENT, 2026-08-27, BEFORE ANY RUN OF THIS FAMILY (no data exists yet, so this is registration rather than post-hoc revision). The `--option-set` analysis mode was built after this file was written. It emits AT MOST one gated comparison per maze per metric (4 tests), and only where the best policy with the structure differs from the best policy without it; where they are the same policy the contribution is exactly 0 by construction and NO gates are computed. Those option-set comparisons are hereby declared MEMBERS OF THE SAME family of 24, not a new family. familySize stays 24 and is NOT narrowed to 4. This is deliberately conservative: padding the BH correction to 24 when 4 or fewer tests are emitted makes every q harder to pass, never easier, so it cannot manufacture a positive. The cost is power, which section 3 of the spec already declares is marginal at this n - and this pilot registers 'no two policies separate' as a valid outcome, so erring toward the null is the correct direction to err in.
